summary: Uber Engineering's Joseph Gilley explains why Uber uses hexagons for geospatial indexing and introduces H3, its open source hierarchical grid system. He covers use cases and how distortion is handled.

title: XDC 2020 - Day 1 - September 16, 2020
summary: Day one of the X.Org Developer's Conference 2020 stream, including talks on the Raspberry Pi 4 Vulkan driver, the WSL graphics architecture, X11 and Wayland apps in WSL, and Mesa for D3D12.

title: Nick Hanauer on inequality
summary: Nick Hanauer's short TED University talk on economic inequality, which was famously not posted on TED's main site at first. He argues that rich people are not the job creators.

title: Clojure is Not Afraid of the GPU - Dragan Djuric
summary: Dragan Djuric presents Clojure libraries for GPU and numerical computing, including ClojureCL, ClojureCUDA and Neanderthal. He shows how a dynamic REPL workflow can be combined with low-level hardware acceleration for machine learning and data science.

title: The artificial gravity lab
summary: Tom Scott tours the rotating room artificial gravity facility at Brandeis University's Graybiel lab. It shows how humans cope with rotation-based gravity and the odd effects such as Coriolis forces.

title: Intelligence is not Enough | Bryan Cantrill | Monktoberfest 2023
summary: Bryan Cantrill's Monktoberfest 2023 talk takes on AI doomerism, weighing the theoretical existential risks against the reality on the ground. He takes a skeptical but thoughtful view of how to balance AI's potential against its risks.

title: 2016 LLVM Developers’ Meeting: D. Dunbar “A New Architecture for Building Software”
summary: Daniel Dunbar of Apple presents llbuild, a framework for building build systems, at the 2016 LLVM Developers' Meeting. He argues that the traditional way C compilers integrate with build systems limits compile speed, and proposes a new architecture.

title: The True Cost of the Royal Family Explained
summary: CGP Grey breaks down what the British Royal Family costs the UK versus what it brings in, including income from royal-owned land. He concludes the government nets a profit from the arrangement.

title: Ion drive: The first flight
summary: Nature video showing MIT researchers flying the first plane with no moving parts, powered by an ion drive that creates an ionic wind from high-powered electrodes. The 5m-wide craft flies across a sports hall.

title: How Japan Learned Semiconductors
summary: Asianometry traces the 30-year rise and peak of Japan's semiconductor industry from the 1950s to the 1980s, covering how a postwar country gained competence in an emerging technology.

title: Can A Metal Bowling Ball Survive Inside a Nuclear Explosion?
summary: Scott Manley explains the Cold War experiments in which steel and aluminium spheres, known as Lew Allen's Balls, were placed near nuclear detonations. The spheres survived the fireball, and he walks through what the declassified results show.

title: Someone improved my code by 40,832,277,770%
summary: Matt Parker follows the community effort to speed up his slow Wordle-solving code, which ended up running hundreds of millions of times faster. He walks through the techniques contributors used.

title: "Design in Practice" by Rich Hickey
summary: Rich Hickey's Clojure Conj 2023 talk on design in practice, covering problem statements, decision matrices, choosing precise words and making decisions in a team.

title: Dutch Cities are Better for the Environment (and my sanity)
summary: Not Just Bikes explains why living in a dense, bikeable Dutch city sharply reduced his family's environmental footprint and improved quality of life. It is a collaboration that continues on Climate Town.

title: Balaji Srinivasan at Startup School 2013
summary: Balaji Srinivasan's Startup School 2013 talk on Silicon Valley's Ultimate Exit, arguing for building alternatives outside existing institutions. It is the primary source for a much-retold and much-distorted idea.

title: Clojure for Lisp Programmers Part 1 - Rich Hickey
summary: Rich Hickey presents an extensive introduction to Clojure at the Boston Lisp meeting, assuming prior Lisp knowledge. It covers the language's design decisions relative to other Lisps.

title: How economic inequality harms societies | Richard Wilkinson
summary: Richard Wilkinson presents data showing that societies with larger income gaps do worse on health, lifespan, trust and other measures. He argues the effects track inequality itself rather than average income. It is a 17-minute TED talk.

title: James Gosling - Simula: a personal journey
summary: James Gosling gives a personal talk at the 50th anniversary seminar of Simula about using the language from 1974 and how it shaped his thinking. He explains how Simula's object model and coroutines influenced the design of Java.

title: The centuries-old debt that's still paying interest
summary: Tom Scott visits Yale's archives to look at a 367-year-old bond from a Dutch water authority that is still paying interest. Finance professor Geert Rouwenhorst explains how it works.

title: The Nuclear Salt Water Rocket - Possibly the Craziest Rocket Engine Ever Imagined.
summary: Scott Manley explains the nuclear salt water rocket, Robert Zubrin's concept of a rocket fueled by a rapid nuclear reaction in uranium salt dissolved in water. He covers its extraordinary performance and the dangers of managing it.

title: How to slow down a stock exchange
summary: Tom Scott visits IEX, a stock exchange that slows down trading with a long coil of fiber. The coil removes the speed advantage of high-frequency traders.

title: The moiré effect lights that guide ships home
summary: Tom Scott investigates moire-effect beacons, called Inogon leading marks, a Swedish invention from the 1980s that shows different patterns depending on the viewer's position. He visits one used to mark an undersea cable and tracks down its history.

title: Peter Munch-Ellingsen: Why I wrote my own keyboard firmware in Nim (NimConf 2021)
summary: Peter Munch-Ellingsen explains at NimConf 2021 why he wrote his own keyboard firmware in Nim instead of using QMK or Arduino. He shows that the resulting firmware is very small.

title: Douglas Crockford: Monads and Gonads (YUIConf Evening Keynote)
summary: Douglas Crockford's YUIConf 2012 evening keynote tries to explain monads in a way programmers can actually understand, in the context of JavaScript. He aims to break the 'monad tutorial curse'.

title: Why the Soviet Computer Failed
summary: An Asianometry explainer on why the Soviet Union, once a leading computing power, fell far behind the US in computers by the 1980s. It traces the gap from the 1960s onward despite strong state support for science.

title: 1,000km Cable to the Stars - The Skyhook
summary: Kurzgesagt explains the skyhook, a rotating cable with a counterweight that could catapult spacecraft from Earth orbit toward deep space. It covers why it would make space travel cheaper and more efficient.

title: Velocity 2011:  Jon Jenkins, "Velocity Culture"
summary: Amazon's Jon Jenkins at Velocity 2011 on how operations can drive revenue and on Amazon's highly available, autonomous architectures. It includes details on deployment frequency and Amazon's move to AWS.

title: AWS re:Invent 2018: Powering Next-Gen EC2 Instances: Deep Dive into the Nitro System (CMP303-R1)
summary: An AWS re:Invent 2018 session diving into the Nitro system, a set of hardware offload and security building blocks behind next-generation EC2 instances. It covers the design and architecture and how Nitro enables new instance types.

title: Model Y E36: The Octovalve Episode
summary: Munro Live's Model Y episode 36 has Sandy Munro walk through the disassembled Tesla Octovalve and heat pump system. He explains how the components are made and what each one does.

title: NYC Tech Talk Series: How Google Backs Up the Internet
summary: A Google Tech Talk by Raymond Blum on how Google backs up massive amounts of data such as Gmail and Picasa. It covers scaling challenges, failure types, and approaches that did not work, including tape.

title: 2013 Keynote: Chandler Carruth: Optimizing the Emergent Structures of C++
summary: Chandler Carruth's CppNow 2013 keynote on how C++ builds complex software from simple emergent structures, and how compilers optimize them through inlining and value semantics.

title: Don Knuth - Constraint Based Composition
summary: Donald Knuth explains at Stanford's CCRMA the constraint-based methods he is using to compose a major work for pipe organ.

title: dotJS 2012 - Brian Leroux - WTFJS
summary: Brian Leroux's dotJS 2012 talk WTFJS is a quick, humorous tour of JavaScript's odd behaviors and quirks.

title: I Did Caffeine Analysis: Some Unexpected Results!
summary: James Hoffmann runs caffeine analyzer tests comparing filter versus espresso, extraction over time, steep time, instant coffee and light versus dark roast.

title: Industrial Strength High Performance RISC V Processors For Energy Efficient Computing
summary: David Ditzel of Esperanto Technologies presents their massively parallel, energy-efficient RISC-V processors at the 7th RISC-V Workshop in 2017. It covers the high-performance many-core design aimed at machine learning.

title: Overview of Illumina Sequencing by Synthesis Workflow | Standard SBS chemistry
summary: Illumina's 3D animation of its sequencing-by-synthesis workflow, from sample preparation and cluster generation to sequencing on a flow cell and data analysis.

title: DeepSec 2010: All your baseband are belong to us by Ralf Philipp Weinmann
summary: A DeepSec 2010 conference talk by Ralf Philipp Weinmann on attacking the baseband processor of mobile phones rather than the application processor. It covers how open-source GSM base stations make malicious-tower attacks practical against neglected GSM stacks.

title: why typing like this is sometimes okay.
summary: Tom Scott makes a short descriptivist argument that language keeps changing and that casual internet writing conventions, like lowercase typing and dropped full stops, are legitimate. It is part of his Language Files series, written with Gretchen McCulloch.

title: Prioritizing Technical Debt as if Time & Money Matters • Adam Tornhill • GOTO 2019
summary: Adam Tornhill's GOTO Copenhagen 2019 talk on how to prioritize technical debt in large codebases. It argues for combining code complexity with change frequency (hotspots) from version control data, rather than trying to quantify debt in the abstract.

title: Stephen Krashen: Language Acquisition and Comprehensible Input
summary: A lecture from the 1980s by linguist Stephen Krashen on how people acquire language. He explains his comprehensible input hypothesis for second-language acquisition.

title: The surprising habits of original thinkers | Adam Grant | TED
summary: Adam Grant's TED talk on the habits of original thinkers, including procrastination and embracing failure. He argues the greatest originals fail the most because they try the most.

title: React.js Conf 2015 - The complementarity of React and Web Components
summary: Andrew Rota of Wayfair argues at React.js Conf 2015 that React and native Web Components complement each other. He shows how they can be combined for complex web applications.

title: PdF 2011 | Eben Moglen: The alternate net we need, and how we can build it ourselves
summary: Eben Moglen's 2011 Personal Democracy Forum talk on the loss of anonymity and privacy on the internet. He proposes building an alternative net of personal servers, the idea behind FreedomBox.

title: I Tried Turning Games Into Text
summary: Acerola explores building a shader that turns games into ASCII art, walking through techniques such as brightness mapping and edge detection to see whether it looks good.

title: Tesla Virtual Power Plant
summary: A QCon London 2020 talk by Tesla engineers on the architecture of Tesla's Virtual Power Plant. It covers aggregating distributed batteries and solar with vertically integrated hardware and software across cloud and edge.

title: An Introduction to SQLite
summary: A 2006 Google TechTalk in which SQLite's author Richard Hipp introduces the embeddable, zero-configuration C database library. He covers its history, strengths and weaknesses, and where it beats client/server databases.

title: Will YouTube Ever Run Out Of Video IDs?
summary: Tom Scott explains YouTube's 11-character video IDs, which are base-64 encoded 64-bit numbers, and whether YouTube could ever run out of them. It covers counting systems and base 64 briefly.

title: Change w/ Jim Keller
summary: Jim Keller, CTO of Tenstorrent, gives a keynote at Stanford's System X conference on change, understanding and the future of computing. He touches on Moore's Law, how far transistors are from physical limits, and ideas like DNA origami.

title: TSP #183 - Starlink Dish Phased Array Design, Architecture & RF In-depth Analysis
summary: The Signal Path takes apart a Starlink dish layer by layer, analyzing the phased array RF design, system architecture and integrated circuits, with an X-ray of the RF stack.

title: The Truth Behind Calorie Labels
summary: Casey Neistat's short New York Times op-doc investigating how accurate restaurant and packaged-food calorie labels really are. He gets items from chains like Chipotle, Starbucks and Subway measured by nutrition researchers and compares them to the printed numbers.

title: Caml Trading
summary: Yaron Minsky explains how Jane Street moved from mainstream languages to developing almost entirely in OCaml. He covers trading systems, research infrastructure, tooling and hiring.

title: DON'T Buy a Used Mining GPU! - $h!t Manufacturers Say
summary: Linus Tech Tips looks at whether buying a used GPU that was previously used for crypto mining is a good idea, as miners prepare to sell off cards. The video discusses how mining affects wear on cards and what to watch for.

title: Inside Hong Kong’s cage homes
summary: A Vox Borders explainer on Hong Kong's housing crisis, the least affordable market in the world, and the tiny cage homes and subdivided flats people squeeze into. It looks at why prices keep climbing and how land policy contributes.

title: Paul Otlet, visioning a web in 1934
summary: A one-minute clip about Paul Otlet, the Belgian bibliographer who in 1934 imagined users accessing a remote database through an electric telescope over a phone line. It presents his vision as a precursor of the web.

title: How a Character LCD works Part 1
summary: The 8-Bit Guy explains how character LCD screens work and how to control them directly, first part of a series.

title: The Extreme World of Ultra Intense Lasers - with Kate Lancaster
summary: Royal Institution lecture by Dr Kate Lancaster on the most powerful lasers in the world and the extreme conditions they create. It includes live demonstrations and covers applications from industry to fusion.

title: The British Museum is full of stolen artifacts
summary: A Vox explainer on how many of the British Museum's treasures were taken during British imperial rule, focusing on the Benin Bronzes and requests for their return.

title: JWST just made the "Crisis in Cosmology" WORSE
summary: Astrophysicist Dr. Becky explains the Hubble tension, the disagreement between expansion-rate measurements from the cosmic microwave background and the distance ladder, and what early JWST Cepheid observations add.

title: Milton Friedman - Case Against Equal Pay for Equal Work
summary: A short clip of Milton Friedman arguing with students that equal pay laws are counterproductive, and that markets penalize discrimination because cheaper equally productive workers are an advantage to hire.

title: Calculating a Car Crash - Numberphile
summary: Numberphile's Ben Sparks works through the physics of a car crash, showing how kinetic energy grows with the square of speed and why stopping distance climbs so quickly as velocity increases.

title: Neural Network Learns The Physics of Fluids and Smoke | Two Minute Papers #118
summary: Two Minute Papers covers a paper on speeding up fluid and smoke simulation with convolutional networks. It contrasts the approach with earlier regression forest methods.

title: BBC - The Code - The Wisdom of the Crowd
summary: Marcus du Sautoy of the BBC demonstrates the wisdom of the crowd, showing that averaging many guesses of jelly beans in a jar lands near the true count.

title: Maciej Ceglowski - The Website Obesity Crisis [Web Directions 2015 Keynote]
summary: Maciej Ceglowski's Web Directions 2015 keynote on website bloat, arguing that pages have grown far heavier than their content justifies. This is a re-upload of the original talk.

title: Blender and Next Gen: a Netflix Original
summary: Jeff Bell's Blender Conference 2018 talk on how Netflix's animated film Next Gen was produced using Blender. It covers the studio's pipeline and tooling.

title: Lessons from a Can Opener
summary: Technology Connections spends 22 minutes on the humble can opener and what its design shows about products and why people don't know what to look for. It uses an everyday tool to draw broader lessons.

title: Lecture 3 - Before the Startup (Paul Graham)
summary: Paul Graham's lecture in the 'How to Start a Startup' course, covering counterintuitive parts of startups and how to have ideas. It is the video form of his essay 'Before the Startup'.

title: Richard Feynman: Can Machines Think?
summary: An excerpt of Richard Feynman's 1985 lecture Q&A about whether machines can think. He discusses the difficulty of defining what computers can never do and compares machine intelligence to machines that don't copy animals.

title: But how do AI images and videos actually work? | Guest video by Welch Labs
summary: A guest video by Welch Labs on 3Blue1Brown explaining how text-to-image and video models work. It covers CLIP, shared embedding spaces, diffusion models (DDPM, DDIM), conditioning, guidance and negative prompts.

title: The EV Detroit is Dying to Benchmark - BYD Seagull
summary: Autoline's John McElroy and Caresoft president Terry Woychowski look at the BYD Seagull, an electric hatchback that sells in China for about $11,500. Woychowski points out the cost-saving design and manufacturing choices, and McElroy takes it for a short test drive.

title: The Secret of Our Success | Joseph Henrich | Talks at Google
summary: Joseph Henrich's Talks at Google presentation of his book. He argues that human success comes from collective brains and cultural learning across generations rather than individual intelligence.

title: Could The Universe Be Inside A Black Hole?
summary: A PBS Space Time episode asking whether our universe could sit inside a black hole. It covers what physicists think happens inside black holes and the arguments for and against this idea.

title: Hybrid Power Split Device. eCVT transmission.
summary: A short animated explanation of the power split device in Toyota-style hybrids, a planetary gearset that works as an eCVT. It shows how engine and motor power are combined.

title: Prof. Robert Lustig - 'Sugar, metabolic syndrome, and cancer'
summary: Pediatric endocrinologist Robert Lustig talks at Low Carb Denver 2020 about sugar, metabolic syndrome and cancer. He lays out the case that metabolic dysfunction drives disease.

title: Rendering Tiny Glades With Entirely Too Much Ray Marching
summary: A Graphics Programming Conference talk on how the game Tiny Glade renders meadows, trees and player-built castles. It covers real-time global illumination, tilt-shift depth of field, stable shadows with continuous time of day, ray marching and GPU-driven rendering on old hardware.

title: What Really Happened at the Oroville Dam Spillway?
summary: Practical Engineering summarizes the 2017 Oroville Dam spillway failure, explaining the engineering details behind the incident. It also discusses how operators and regulators failed to keep downstream residents safe.

title: David Patterson - A New Golden Age for Computer Architecture: History, Challenges and Opportunities
summary: David Patterson's talk on the history of computer architecture, from RISC and superscalar designs to the end of Dennard scaling and Moore's Law. It argues that domain-specific architectures and open instruction sets open a new golden age.

title: Velocity 2010:  James Hamilton, "Datacenter Infrastructure Innovation"
summary: James Hamilton of AWS gives a Velocity 2010 keynote on datacenter infrastructure innovation, focused on power and cooling costs and a breakdown of where datacenter spending goes.

title: Compiling and Optimizing Scripting Languages
summary: Paul Biggar's Google Tech Talk on compiling and optimizing scripting languages, drawn from his work on the phc ahead-of-time PHP compiler. He covers runtime typing, aliasing and code generation challenges, and argues AOT can compete with JIT.

title: Why Parallel Universes Are Probably Real
summary: Veritasium explains the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics, drawing heavily on Sean Carroll's book. It walks through the Schrodinger equation and why wave collapse may be unnecessary if the universe keeps splitting.

title: RailsConf 2011: Aaron Patterson, "Double Dream Hands: So Intense!"
summary: Aaron Patterson's RailsConf 2011 talk on Rails 3.1 performance, showing why deeper Rack middleware stacks slow Rails and how a shallower pipeline helps. It also touches on Rack API design.

title: ATP synthase in action
summary: A short Harvard Online animation, narrated by Professor Rob Lue, showing how ATP synthase works inside mitochondria. It comes from the HarvardX Cell Biology: Mitochondria course.

title: This Tiny Island has Insane Traffic
summary: Not Just Bikes looks at traffic in the Bahamas to show that a small country can be just as car-centric as a big one. He ties it to land use, car dependence and how dedicated transit lanes help.

title: The Genius of 3D Printed Rockets
summary: A Veritasium video touring Relativity Space and explaining why 3D printing whole rockets cuts tooling costs, allows rapid iteration, reduces part count and enables new designs. It includes an interview with Scott Manley on aerospace engineering.

title: Lines of Light: How Analog Television Works
summary: Technology Connections explains how analog television produced moving images without computers, covering scanning, CRTs and standards like NTSC and PAL. It is part of a series on analog TV.

title: React without memo
summary: A React Conf talk by Xuan Huang previewing React Forget, a compiler that automatically memoizes components. It argues for making memoization the default so developers need not write useMemo or useCallback by hand.

title: The Memory Sinkhole - Unleashing An X86 Design Flaw Allowing Universal Privilege Escalation
summary: Christopher Domas's Black Hat 2015 talk on a long-unnoticed x86 design flaw that lets an attacker reach System Management Mode, a ring below the OS. It explains how the legacy architecture allows universal privilege escalation and persistent, hard-to-detect malware.

title: seL4 Is Free – What Does This Mean For You?
summary: Gernot Heiser presents seL4, a microkernel with a mathematical proof connecting security properties to the binary code, and explains what its open-sourcing means for users. It covers its roles as a microkernel, separation kernel and hypervisor.

title: Anathem | Neal Stephenson | Talks at Google
summary: Neal Stephenson visits Google in 2008 to discuss his novel Anathem as part of the Authors@Google series. He talks about the book's world and takes audience questions.

title: Mach-E Thermal System Part 2: A Detailed Comparison to the Model Y
summary: Munro Live's team breaks down the thermal management system of the Ford Mustang Mach-E and compares it with the Tesla Model Y. They look at parts count, coolant loops and heating approaches.

title: The Most Dangerous Stretch of Water in the World: The Strid at Bolton Abbey, Yorkshire
summary: Tom Scott visits the Strid at Bolton Abbey in Yorkshire, a deceptively narrow stretch of river with dangerous currents. He covers its reputation and the 12th-century legend of the Boy of Egremont.

title: Bertrand's Paradox (with 3blue1brown) - Numberphile
summary: Numberphile interviews Grant Sanderson of 3blue1brown about Bertrand's paradox, where different reasonable ways of picking a random chord of a circle give different probabilities.

title: 2018 LLVM Developers’ Meeting:  C. Schafmeister “Lessons Learned Implementing Common Lisp with LLVM”
summary: Christian Schafmeister presents lessons from six years of implementing Clasp, a Common Lisp compiler using LLVM as its backend that interoperates with C++. He explains handling a dynamic, memory-managed language on LLVM.

title: Optical illusions show how we see | Beau Lotto
summary: Neuroscientist Beau Lotto runs the audience through color and pattern illusions to show that perception is shaped by context and evolutionary history rather than being a direct readout of the world. The talk is playful and hands-on, and it argues that the brain interprets ambiguous signals.

title: New NES Tetris Technique: Faster Than Hypertapping!
summary: aGameScout explains rolling, the third major NES Tetris playstyle, in which players tap the back of the controller to move pieces faster than hypertapping. It covers how the technique works and where it comes from.

title: Restoring the ancient Caledonian Forest Alan Watson Featherstone TEDxFindhorn
summary: Alan Watson Featherstone, founder of Trees for Life, describes nearly 30 years of work restoring the ancient Caledonian Forest in the Scottish Highlands, illustrated with his photography.

title: Making an international standard cup of tea
summary: Tom Scott follows the ISO 3103 / BS 6008 standard to make an international standard cup of tea, using specialist tasting equipment. The video shows how precisely the standard is specified.

title: T-Mobile’s path to IPv6 Only
summary: A Rocky Mountain IPv6 Taskforce talk in which T-Mobile's Stephan Lagerholm explains how the carrier went IPv6-only using DNS64 and 464XLAT, with a live Android demo and best practices.

title: BadUSB - On Accessories that Turn Evil by Karsten Nohl + Jakob Lell
summary: Karsten Nohl and Jakob Lell present BadUSB at Black Hat 2014, showing that USB controller firmware can be reprogrammed to impersonate other device types. They demonstrate system compromise and a self-replicating USB threat that current defenses cannot detect.

title: Elliptic Curve Back Door - Computerphile
summary: Dr Mike Pound explains the suspected backdoor in the Dual_EC_DRBG random number generator and how elliptic curve constants could let someone predict its output.

title: Wim Hof breathing tutorial by Wim Hof
summary: Wim Hof guides viewers step by step through his breathing method, with some explanation of the science he cites behind it. It stresses learning from the source and avoiding unsafe settings.

title: Feynman :: Rules of Chess
summary: A three-minute clip of Richard Feynman using the rules of chess as an analogy for how science works, discovering rules by observation and sometimes meeting surprises like castling. It touches on incremental progress versus revolutions.

title: Why do YouTube views freeze at 301?
summary: Numberphile visits YouTube to learn why view counts on new videos used to freeze at 301. It explains that YouTube holds counts while it verifies views aren't from bots or fakes.

title: The Principles of Clean Architecture by Uncle Bob Martin
summary: Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob) presents the principles of Clean Architecture, covering dependency direction, boundaries, and why frameworks and databases should be details rather than the center of an application.

title: How H&M’s Recycling Machines Make New Clothes From Used Apparel | World Wide Waste
summary: A Business Insider World Wide Waste episode on H&M's garment recycling machines, which turn used clothing into new apparel. It asks whether a fast fashion company can solve the waste problem it helped create.

title: EEVblog #632 - Solar Roadways Are RUBBISH!
summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog debunks the Solar Roadways project, which raised millions through Indiegogo and government funding. He works through the solar generation and LED power calculations to show the idea isn't viable.

title: Will Wright GDC 2005 Spore (The Future of Content) Remastered
summary: A remastered recording of Will Wright's 2005 GDC talk revealing Spore, titled The Future of Content. He covers procedurally generated content and the ambitions of the game, with gameplay demo starting around 12:30.

title: You Need to Be Bored. Here's Why.
summary: Harvard professor Arthur Brooks explains why boredom is useful rather than something to avoid. He describes how a wandering mind engages the brain's default mode network, which supports creativity and curiosity, and suggests it may protect against depression.

title: Why Can't we Remake the Rocketdyne F1 Engine?
summary: Short Curious Droid video on why NASA could not simply rebuild the Saturn V's Rocketdyne F-1 engine for the SLS boosters. It explains that the engines were hand-tailored and that much of the know-how was never documented, so the blueprints were not enough.

title: All Tube Stations Have Fifteen Floors
summary: Geoff Marshall explains a running gag about London Underground stair signs claiming that the climb equals 15 floors, regardless of how many steps there actually are.

title: VCF East: Xerox Star vs. Apple Lisa
summary: Jason Perkins's talk at Vintage Computer Festival East 2020 compares the user interface of the Xerox Star with that of the Apple Lisa. It covers editing documents, the Star's mouse and a Q&A.

title: I published music on Tidal to test MQA - MQA Review
summary: GoldenSound publishes music on Tidal to test MQA, a deep dive into the format's claims and problems including its leaky filter. Testing begins around the 5:45 mark.

title: Linux for Chromebooks: Secure Development (Google I/O ’19)
summary: A Google I/O 2019 talk explaining the architecture of Linux on Chromebooks (Crostini), a sandboxed Linux development environment built on containers inside a VM, with demos and design rationale.

title: The city of golf carts
summary: Tom Scott visits Peachtree City, Georgia, which has about a hundred miles of dedicated golf cart paths that serve as an alternative to driving. He explains how the network works as a quasi-transit system that keeps cars off the roads.

title: Inno-Versity Presents: Greatness by David Marquet
summary: Retired submarine captain David Marquet explains, with drawings, how he turned the USS Santa Fe around by treating his crew as leaders rather than followers. It summarizes the ideas of his book Turn the Ship Around.

title: Google I/O 2008 - Dalvik Virtual Machine Internals
summary: Dan Bornstein's Google I/O 2008 talk on the internals of Dalvik, the virtual machine that runs Android code. It covers the motivation for its design, the dex format and its register-based interpreter, plus tips for writing code that suits the platform.

title: Beware, fellow plutocrats, the pitchforks are coming | Nick Hanauer
summary: Billionaire Nick Hanauer warns fellow wealthy people in a TED talk that growing inequality could lead to social upheaval like pre-revolutionary France. He argues a higher minimum wage would grow the middle class and prosperity.

title: Why We Run FreeBSD current at Netflix – Drew Gallatin
summary: Netflix engineer Drew Gallatin explains why the company runs FreeBSD-current on its CDN. He describes the team, how they track upstream, their contributions and performance milestones, and a bug causing a 20% performance regression.

title: Epicycles, complex Fourier series and Homer Simpson's orbit
summary: Mathologer explains epicycles and complex Fourier series, inspired by an animation of Homer Simpson drawn with epicycles. It covers the shape of the Moon's orbit around the Sun and how to make your own epicycle drawings.

title: The Best-Designed Town in the Netherlands (and therefore, the world)
summary: Not Just Bikes tours Houten, a Dutch town designed around cycling, explaining how its layout makes most trips by bike safe and easy. It also promotes a book about the town.

title: Laniakea: Our home supercluster
summary: A short Nature video on the discovery that our home supercluster is Laniakea, redefined by mapping the flow of galaxies rather than their density. It names the structure with a Hawaiian word meaning 'immeasurable heaven'.

title: Reveal Invisible Motion With This Clever Video Trick
summary: Steve Mould explains motion amplification and video magnification, techniques that find tiny changes in video invisible to the eye and exaggerate them. He covers the MIT research and industrial uses such as diagnosing vibrating machinery.

title: The Go Programming Language
summary: Rob Pike's October 2009 Google Tech Talk introducing Go, a new experimental systems language designed for fast builds, concurrency and garbage collection. It covers the goals, syntax and type system.

title: Human AI is Decades Away, But We Need to Start the Debate Now | Demis Hassabis | Google Zeitgeist
summary: Demis Hassabis of DeepMind speaks at Google Zeitgeist, saying human-level AI is decades away but the debate should start now. He covers DeepMind's focus on game-playing agents.

title: Understanding Specter: Clojure's missing piece
summary: A screencast tutorial on Specter, a Clojure library for navigating and transforming nested data structures declaratively, demonstrated in a REPL.

title: Politics and Language | Noam Chomsky | Talks at Google
summary: Noam Chomsky gives a Talks at Google lecture covering his work on politics and language. It touches on his linguistic theory, including universal grammar, alongside his political criticism.

title: Swift for TensorFlow: The Next-Generation Machine Learning Framework (TF Dev Summit '19)
summary: Chris Lattner and Brennan Saeta present Swift for TensorFlow at the TensorFlow Dev Summit 2019, covering language-integrated automatic differentiation and tooling for machine learning in Swift.

title: How to (Quickly) Build a Cycling City - Paris
summary: Not Just Bikes visits Paris to see how Mayor Anne Hidalgo's policies are turning it into a '100% cyclable' city. It looks at the changes that took space from cars for bikes and people.

title: Copyrighting all the melodies to avoid accidental infringement | Damien Riehl | TEDxMinneapolis
summary: Lawyer and musician Damien Riehl argues that music is math with a finite number of melodies, and describes how he and programmer Noah Rubin generated every possible melody and released them under CC0 to avoid accidental infringement claims.

title: Making YBCO superconductor
summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science shows how to make and test YBCO high-temperature superconductor with a kiln and eBay chemicals. He demonstrates flux pinning and shows a close-up of the crystal structure.

title: Obesity is a National Security Issue: Lieutenant General Mark Hertling at TEDxMidAtlantic 2012
summary: Lieutenant General Mark Hertling gives a TEDx talk arguing that obesity and poor youth fitness are a national security problem because too few young Americans can meet military physical requirements.

title: Google I/O 2012 - Meet the Go Team
summary: A fireside Q&A with the Go team (Pike, Thompson, Griesemer and others) at Google I/O 2012. They answer audience questions about Go's design, goals, garbage collection plans and future.

title: DEFCON 20: Bigger Monster, Weaker Chains: The National Security Agency and the Constitution
summary: A DEFCON 20 panel with NSA whistleblower William Binney, journalist James Bamford and ACLU lawyers on the NSA's mass collection of communications and its conflict with the Constitution.

title: MMO Economies - Hyperinflation, Reserve Currencies & You! - Extra Credits
summary: An Extra Credits episode on how MMO economies get overrun by inflation when players can mint unlimited gold by killing monsters. It covers approaches borrowed from real-world economics, such as anchoring or pegging currency, as alternatives to simple gold sinks.

title: The Surprising Secret of Synchronization
summary: Veritasium explores how synchronization arises spontaneously in nature, with metronomes, fireflies and bridges, drawing on Steven Strogatz's work on chaos and complexity.

title: HOW TO DATAMOSH: PART 1
summary: A how-to video on datamoshing, the glitch-art technique of removing keyframes so that motion data smears across video. It walks through the tools needed, such as ffmpegx and Avidemux, though the author notes parts are outdated.

title: Ken Stanley: Discovery Without Objectives
summary: A 92-minute RMIT University seminar in which Ken Stanley argues that setting an objective can block achieving it. He presents objective-less, novelty-driven search as an alternative approach to innovation and discovery, drawing on evolutionary computation.

title: Why is India so filthy? | The Ugly Indian | TEDxBangalore
summary: A TEDxBangalore talk by The Ugly Indian, an anonymous collective, asking why Indians tolerate filthy public spaces. It describes their volunteer approach of quietly cleaning up spots and turning the tragedy of the commons into a victory.

title: October CincyRb - Jim Weirich on Decoupling from Rails
summary: A Cincinnati Ruby meetup talk by Jim Weirich on decoupling application logic from Rails. He argues for separating business logic from framework and database models.

title: Chris Urmson: How a driverless car sees the road
summary: Chris Urmson, head of Google's self-driving car program, shows footage of how the car perceives the road and decides what to do. Examples include cyclist hand signals, school buses, police officers and complex intersections.

title: How to Win an Interstellar War
summary: A Kurzgesagt video exploring how advanced civilizations might wage war across light years. It looks at weapons such as relativistic beams and what they would do.

title: This clock was famous, but the internet ruined it.
summary: Tom Scott explains the famous Dutch flower auction clock at Royal FloraHolland in Aalsmeer, a literal Dutch auction, and how the internet changed it. It is a short look at how the system worked then and now.

title: How Physicists Created a Holographic Wormhole in a Quantum Computer
summary: Quanta Magazine explains the 2022 experiment that claimed to create a holographic wormhole on Google's quantum computer. The description now notes that a later independent analysis questioned whether any wormhole was created.

title: The Weird World in RGB
summary: Technology Connections explains how RGB light and color work, from hue and saturation to color vision and how objects appear under different lighting. It uses a studio setup with colored lights to demonstrate the effects.

title: NixOS VM on Mac Setup
summary: Mitchell Hashimoto walks through his setup for running a NixOS virtual machine on a Mac as his development environment, with a config repo on GitHub.

title: Multithreading the Entire Destiny Engine
summary: A 2015 GDC talk by Bungie's Barry Genova on how Destiny's engine was restructured into a job graph with limited thread pre-emption. It is aimed at programmers of demanding game engines.

title: Martin Kleppmann | Kafka Summit SF 2018 Keynote (Is Kafka a Database?)
summary: Martin Kleppmann's Kafka Summit 2018 keynote asks whether Kafka can be considered a database. He covers event logs and related data-systems ideas.

title: Scaling ZFS for NVMe - Allan Jude - EuroBSDcon 2022
summary: Allan Jude of Klara presents work on making ZFS scale on fast NVMe storage, covering fixes to the TaskQueue interface and removal of bottlenecks. The talk was given at EuroBSDcon 2022 and describes raising write throughput from about 3 to over 7 GB/sec.

title: The nightmare videos of childrens' YouTube — and what's wrong with the internet today | James Bridle
summary: Writer and artist James Bridle shows how strange and disturbing children's videos on YouTube, from surprise eggs to algorithmic mashups, are produced for ad revenue. He argues they reveal problems in a data-driven internet.

title: CppCon 2016: Chandler Carruth “High Performance Code 201: Hybrid Data Structures"
summary: Chandler Carruth's CppCon 2016 talk on designing hybrid data structures for performance. He covers cache locality, working-set size and allocation overhead, and why standard C++ containers fall short.

title: Steve Yegge, "What Would You Do With Your Own Google?" - OSCON Data 2011
summary: Steve Yegge's OSCON Data 2011 talk imagines what you could do with Google-scale storage and compute a decade later. He argues smart people should work on hard problems such as biology rather than cat pictures, and the talk ends with a moment many took as him quitting Google.

title: We Need to Rethink Exercise (Updated Version)
summary: Kurzgesagt explains why exercise alone does little for weight loss, since the body compensates by adjusting its total energy expenditure. It argues exercise is still very valuable for health.

title: The Trains that Subsidize Suburbia - GO Transit Commuter Rail
summary: Not Just Bikes examines Toronto's GO Transit commuter rail, arguing it is a costly system with park-and-ride stations and rush-hour-only service that subsidizes car-dependent suburbs.

title: What if Humans Are NOT Earth's First Civilization? | Silurian Hypothesis
summary: PBS Space Time examines the Silurian hypothesis, the idea that an industrial civilization could have existed on Earth before humans. It looks at what traces such a civilization might leave in the geological record.

title: How to Make/Build a Lifter or Ionocraft
summary: A step-by-step guide to building a lifter, a small triangular ionocraft made from balsa wood, aluminum foil and thin wire, powered by a high-voltage supply. It also shows high-voltage safety practices.

title: I built a QR code with my bare hands to see how it works
summary: Veritasium builds a QR code by hand to explain how it works. It covers the history of Morse code and barcodes, how QR codes encode data, why damaged codes still scan, and how safe they are.

title: The synthesis of imagination: Rony Abovitz and Magic Leap at TEDxSarasota
summary: A surreal multimedia TEDxSarasota performance by Magic Leap founder Rony Abovitz, held on 12/12/12, mixing performance art with talk about imagination and creativity.

title: Black Hat USA 2013 - Spy-Jacking the Booters
summary: Brian Krebs and Lance James present research on DDoS booter services at Black Hat 2013, including the SWATting Krebs suffered. HN knows it mainly for a later exchange between Krebs and Cloudflare's Matthew Prince.

title: Is the Universe a Simulation? | 2016 Isaac Asimov Memorial Debate
summary: The 2016 Isaac Asimov Memorial Debate, moderated by Neil deGrasse Tyson, in which a panel of physicists and philosophers debates whether the universe is a simulation. Participants include David Chalmers, Zohreh Davoudi and James Gates.

title: Bonhoeffer‘s Theory of Stupidity
summary: An animated Sprouts video presenting Dietrich Bonhoeffer's argument that stupidity is more dangerous than evil, because reason cannot reach stupid people. It frames stupidity as a social and moral phenomenon.

title: The Uncracked Problem with 33 - Numberphile
summary: Numberphile with Tim Browning on the sum-of-three-cubes problem and why 33 was the lowest unsolved case. The description notes a later solution for 33.

title: Steve Jobs Introducing The iPhone At MacWorld 2007
summary: Steve Jobs's January 2007 MacWorld keynote segment introducing the original iPhone. He presents it as a widescreen iPod, a phone and an internet communicator in one device.

title: Experiences Building Edge TPU with Chisel
summary: A Google talk from the Chisel community in which engineers recount designing the Edge TPU with the Chisel hardware construction language. It covers the productivity gains and the problems they hit.

title: Why PlayStation 1 Graphics Warped and Wobbled so much | MVG
summary: Modern Vintage Gamer explains why PlayStation 1 graphics warped and jittered, comparing it with the Nintendo 64. The causes are affine texture mapping and the lack of sub-pixel vertex precision.

title: Elon Musk's Unbelievably Simple 12-minute Killer Break Down on Climate Change
summary: Elon Musk gives students at the Sorbonne a short, simple explanation of climate change and carbon emissions shortly before the 2015 COP21 conference in Paris. He covers why CO2 accumulation matters and argues for a carbon tax.

title: How Much Is a Human Worth? (according to engineers)
summary: Practical Engineering explains how engineers and agencies put a dollar value on a human life to weigh cost against safety. It covers the legal and regulatory basis for these calculations.

title: Inventing the Computer Mouse | Douglas Engelbart | Talks at Google
summary: A Talks at Google visit by Douglas Engelbart, inventor of the mouse. He presents his lifelong aim of augmenting collective human intelligence, followed by a Q&A.

title: Building the Software 2 0 Stack (Andrej Karpathy)
summary: Andrej Karpathy's Databricks talk on Software 2.0, the shift from human-written code to code produced by neural network training. It covers how developer work moves toward curating datasets, the advantages and challenges, and opportunities for new tooling.

title: Feynman: How the train stays on the track  FUN TO IMAGINE 7
summary: A short clip from the 1983 BBC series Fun to Imagine in which Richard Feynman explains how a train stays on the track. He covers the geometry of tapered wheels that steer the train back toward the center of the rails.

title: Tesla Autopilot Crashes into Motorcycle Riders - Why?
summary: FortNine looks at why Tesla Autopilot has rear-ended motorcyclists, speculating that the vision system misreads motorcycle taillights as a distant car. It argues that radar and other sensors would help.

title: How to Stop a Riot
summary: Wendover Productions explains counterintuitive riot control techniques based on research, showing that effective tactics tend to avoid violence.

title: 英特尔Lunar Lake深度评测：轻薄本有救了！
summary: Geekerwan's Chinese-language review of Intel's Lunar Lake lightweight laptop chip, covering performance, perf-per-watt curves and battery life benchmarks. It tests whether x86 can compete on efficiency.

title: WORLD'S BEST AIR FRIES (Weird Trick, But It Works!)
summary: Chef Chris Young shows a simplified triple-cooked method for making crisp frozen fries in an air fryer, based on Heston Blumenthal's technique.

title: LCCS: The LCD / CRT Hybrid from JVC
summary: A Technology Connections video on JVC's LCCS, a display hybrid that cycles a color LCD shutter over a monochrome CRT to produce field-sequential color without dots or stripes. It builds on his earlier videos about analog TV and compatible color.

title: Inbox Zero
summary: Merlin Mann's 2007 Google Tech Talk on Inbox Zero, covering Getting Things Done, why an empty inbox matters, and strategies for handling high-volume email. It is a talk on attention and processing mail rather than on emptying it for its own sake.

title: xkcd | Randall Munroe | Talks at Google
summary: Randall Munroe, creator of xkcd, gives an Authors@Google talk in 2007 about the webcomic and his background, followed by audience Q&A. Donald Knuth and Guido van Rossum ask questions during the session.

title: Konstantin Kisin: Woke Culture HAS Gone Too Far - 7/8 | Oxford Union
summary: A speech by comedian Konstantin Kisin at an Oxford Union debate on whether woke culture has gone too far. He argues the case in a short segment of the debate.

title: SICP / What is "Computer Science" ?
summary: An excerpt from Hal Abelson's opening SICP lecture introducing computer science and contrasting declarative and imperative knowledge. He argues that computer science is not really a science and is more like magic or engineering of ideas.

title: How to replicate Teenage Engineering OP-1 and OP-1 Field for free. | GAS Therapy #35
summary: A tutorial in the GAS Therapy series showing how to recreate the Teenage Engineering OP-1 and OP-1 Field with free software. It argues you do not need to buy expensive gear to make music.

title: We Were Right! Real Inner Misalignment
summary: Robert Miles covers a paper where researchers ran real versions of his earlier mesa-optimizer thought experiments. They show inner misalignment, where an AI learns the wrong goal in training and misbehaves when deployed.

title: Coroutines and Loom behind the scenes by Roman Elizarov
summary: Roman Elizarov compares Kotlin Coroutines with OpenJDK Project Loom virtual threads, looking at their design goals and how those translate into different implementations and tradeoffs. He addresses how the two can coexist.

title: Condition Systems in an Exceptional Language - Chris Houser
summary: Chris Houser's Clojure/conj talk on why Clojure's exceptions destroy information as the stack unwinds, unlike Common Lisp's condition system, which can resume from the error site. He surveys the existing libraries that approximate conditions, explains why they don't compose with each other, and considers what a better design would look like.

title: Why Railroads Don't Need Expansion Joints
summary: Practical Engineering explains how continuous welded rail copes with thermal expansion by restraining it, using the relationship between temperature, stress and strain. The video is part of a series on railways.

title: Even Small Towns are Great Here (5 Years in the Netherlands)
summary: Not Just Bikes reflects on five years in the Netherlands and tours small towns and cities, from Haarlem to Veenendaal. It argues that good urbanism with walkable streets, bike infrastructure and transit is found almost everywhere there, not just in Amsterdam.

title: React.js Conf 2016 - Ben Alpert - What Lies Ahead
summary: Ben Alpert of the React team talks at React.js Conf 2016 about where React is heading. He covers performance and stability work, challenges at Facebook, and opportunities such as bringing React Native ideas to the web.

title: Google I/O 2011: Writing Web Apps in Go
summary: A Google I/O 2011 talk by Andrew Gerrand and Rob Pike on building and deploying a web application in Go. It argues that Go offers speed, reliability and simplicity together.

title: Keynote: KubeCon Opening Keynote - Kelsey Hightower, Google
summary: Kelsey Hightower's opening keynote at KubeCon, delivered as a live-demo style talk about Kubernetes and cloud-native tooling.

title: Uncovered - Dangerous Secrets of the DOT Helmet Standard
summary: FortNine argues that the US DOT motorcycle helmet standard (FMVSS 218) is badly outdated and weak. It compares it with Snell and ECE standards and points to where you can look up test reports for your own helmet.

title: Lecture 7A | MIT 6.001 Structure and Interpretation, 1986
summary: Lecture 7A of the 1986 MIT 6.001 SICP course, with Gerald Sussman presenting the metacircular evaluator, part 1. It shows how a Lisp evaluator can be written in Lisp itself.

title: Destiny's Multithreaded Rendering Architecture
summary: A GDC 2015 talk in which Natalya Tatarchuk describes the multithreaded renderer Bungie built for Destiny. It covers the low-latency architecture across platforms, its successes and its challenges.

title: UPDATED: How to: Reset C by GE Light Bulbs
summary: GE Lighting's official how-to for factory resetting C by GE smart bulbs, using a long sequence of precisely timed on and off cycles.

title: The 2.7% Rule for Retirement Spending
summary: Ben Felix examines whether the well-known 4% retirement withdrawal rule holds up, drawing on academic papers. He argues that a safe rate may be closer to 2.7%, especially for early retirees.

title: [OUTDATED 2018 INSTRUCTIONS] HOW TO USE THE WINDSHIELD WIPERS // TESLA MODEL 3
summary: A 2018 vlog showing how to use the windshield wipers on a Tesla Model 3, including auto mode, manual settings and voice commands. It is labeled outdated.

title: Microsoft is Getting Rusty: A Review of Successes and Challenges - Mark Russinovich
summary: Mark Russinovich's closing keynote at Rust Nation UK on Microsoft's adoption of Rust, covering security gains, integration challenges, performance results and lessons learned.

title: Which country does the most good for the world? | Simon Anholt
summary: Policy advisor Simon Anholt presents the Good Country Index, a measure of how much each nation contributes to the world beyond its own borders. In a funny TED talk he argues governments should think globally, and reveals which countries rank surprisingly.

title: John Carmack Keynote QuakeCon 2010 Part 1
summary: Audio-only recording of the first part of John Carmack's QuakeCon 2010 keynote, taken from G4TV. It covers id Software's work around that time, including Rage and platform topics such as PC, PS3 and Xbox 360, and includes his informal audience poll about paying for mobile apps.

title: Intel ME explained (intel management engine) from insider
summary: A short video explaining the Intel Management Engine, a hidden embedded computer inside Intel machines with deep access to hardware. It is presented from an insider's perspective and raises backdoor and NSA concerns.

title: USA's Leading Dissident Voice | Noam Chomsky | Talks at Google
summary: Noam Chomsky speaks at Google Cambridge in 2017 about his political development and the control of information and media. It is a wide-ranging talk with audience discussion.

title: Are You Eating a Credit Card Every Week?
summary: A vlogbrothers video tracing how the claim that people eat a credit card of plastic every week spread. It walks through the funded talking point, the misleading amplification, and the peer review that missed it.

title: Bitcoin Q&A: Energy Consumption
summary: Andreas Antonopoulos answers a Bitcoin Q&A question about energy consumption in mining. He argues that mining is arbitrage for the cheapest electricity, drives investment in renewables, and that the traditional financial system has hidden externalities.

title: How to charge your non-Tesla at a Supercharger and what NOT to do!
summary: A guide to charging a non-Tesla EV, here a BMW i4, at a Tesla Supercharger in the UK, with do's and don'ts. It shows the process in practice now that the network is open to all cars.

title: One Hacker Way Rational alternative of Agile -  Erik Meijer
summary: Erik Meijer gives a provocative talk presenting what he calls a rational alternative to Agile, arguing against Scrum-style practice. He also touches on the tenth-man concept.

title: Vertical Landing Rockets Before SpaceX
summary: Curious Droid surveys vertical take-off and landing rockets that predate SpaceX and Blue Origin, including the McDonnell Douglas DC-X of the 1990s. It shows that propulsive landing has about 60 years of history.

title: What Happens When Ammo Burns? Sporting Ammunition and the Fire Fighter | SAAMI.org
summary: A SAAMI-produced training video for firefighters explaining what happens when sporting ammunition burns, including that unchambered cartridges lack the energy to penetrate much. It includes test footage of ammunition in fires.

title: Dutch junction design - safer for cyclists
summary: A short BicycleDutch episode showing how Dutch junctions with protected cycle paths are laid out. It argues these are proven, non-experimental designs that make intersections safer for cyclists.

title: Can GPT-4 translate literature?
summary: Tom Gally, a former professional translator and University of Tokyo professor, discusses in March 2023 whether GPT-4 and similar models could translate literary and popular fiction. He gives his assessment of Japanese-to-English quality.

title: Wiretapping the Secret Service can be easy and fun | Bryan Seely | TEDxKirkland
summary: Bryan Seely tells how he used fake Google Maps business listings to intercept phone calls meant for the Secret Service and FBI. He then turned himself in, and the talk explains the verification gaps that made it possible.

title: Adventure with Types in Haskell - Simon Peyton Jones (Lecture 1)
summary: Simon Peyton Jones's first lecture on types in Haskell from the Oregon Programming Languages Summer School 2013. It covers type classes and how they relate to OOP, subtyping and polymorphism.

title: Britain's largest battery is actually a lake
summary: Tom Scott visits Dinorwig Power Station in Wales, a pumped-storage hydro plant often called Britain's largest battery. He explains how it works and how its role has shifted from TV pickup spikes to balancing wind and solar.

title: Why all solar panels are secretly LEDs (and all LEDs are secretly solar panels)
summary: Steve Mould shows that LEDs and solar panels are both diodes made from semiconductors, so a solar panel can emit light and an LED can generate electricity. He demonstrates a small solar panel lighting up.

title: White holes and wormholes are probably real. Here's why.
summary: Veritasium explores what general relativity says about black holes, white holes and wormholes, with help from physicists Geraint Lewis and Juan Maldacena. It introduces Penrose diagrams and the idea that other universes may be implied.

title: !!Con 2020 - Playing Breakout… inside a PDF!! by Omar Rizwan
summary: Omar Rizwan's short !!Con talk about writing a Breakout game in JavaScript that runs inside a PDF. It explores the surprisingly large PDF specification, including its scripting support.

title: CppCon 2018: Nicolai Josuttis “The Nightmare of Initialization in C++”
summary: Nicolai Josuttis's CppCon 2018 talk walks through the many forms of initialization in C++, including uniform initialization, and how their rules and effects differ. He argues the situation is confusing enough that nobody can say what to teach beginners.

title: AWS re:Invent 2017: How Netflix Tunes Amazon EC2 Instances for Performance (CMP325)
summary: A Netflix performance engineer presents how Netflix tunes EC2 instances, covering instance type choice, Xen modes, SR-IOV and kernel tuning. The goal is near bare-metal performance in the cloud.

title: Elements of Programming Style - Brian Kernighan
summary: Brian Kernighan's 2009 talk at Princeton on the Elements of Programming Style, discussing readable code, avoiding cleverness and flawed examples in programming tutorials.

title: Let's prototype a JavaScript JIT compiler!
summary: Andreas Kling live-codes a prototype JavaScript JIT compiler for the LibJS engine used in SerenityOS and Ladybird. He builds a standalone bytecode VM, a simple interpreter, and then a simple JIT in about 80 minutes.

title: Protected KVM on Arm64: A Technical Deep Dive - Quentin Perret, Google
summary: Quentin Perret of Google gives a technical deep dive into protected KVM (pKVM) on Arm64, a confidential computing approach for CPUs without hardware extensions. It explains how the nVHE hypervisor manages stage-2 MMU access control to protect guest memory.

title: Satoshi Has No Clothes: Failures in On-Chain Privacy by Ian Miers (Devcon4)
summary: Ian Miers' Devcon4 talk on failures in on-chain privacy for Bitcoin and Ethereum. It covers attacks on transparent and decoy-based schemes, including how Monero-style privacy can be eroded over repeated transactions.

title: Rust: A Language for the Next 40 Years - Carol Nichols
summary: Carol Nichols' Philly ETE 2019 talk on what makes Rust unique. It covers memory safety, how editions let the language evolve without breaking code, and who relies on Rust in production.

title: An Observation on Generalization
channel: Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing
summary: Ilya Sutskever gives a Simons Institute talk on why neural networks generalize, framing learning as finding short descriptions, like compression. It was part of the Large Language Models and Transformers program.

title: The high cost of free parking
summary: A Vox explainer on how mandatory parking minimums and free parking impose hidden costs on cities. It draws on Donald Shoup's work and gives the history of parking requirements.

title: What Happened When This City Banned Housing Investors
summary: Oh The Urbanity! tests the theory that banning housing investors would fix affordability, using Rotterdam's ban as a case study. The video finds mixed results.

title: The magic washing machine | Hans Rosling
summary: Hans Rosling makes the case that the washing machine was the greatest invention of the industrial revolution. Using Gapminder graphics, he shows how electricity and economic growth free up time for reading and learning.

title: Negative Ion/Anti-5g Products Are Actually RADIOACTIVE
summary: The Thought Emporium tests so-called negative ion and anti-5G wellness products and finds they are radioactive, with some coated in powdered thorium.

title: Mastering Chaos - A Netflix Guide to Microservices
summary: A QCon talk from Netflix on running a large microservices architecture and building resilience into it. It touches on tooling such as Hystrix and circuit breakers.

title: Will We Ever Run Out of New Music?
summary: Vsauce asks whether music will ever run out of new melodies. It counts the possible note combinations and discusses how common chord progressions and remixing affect originality.

title: Putting Google's Network to work for You
summary: A seven-minute Google I/O 2014 talk by Simon Newton on how developers can make use of Google's global network. It describes the network's footprint and some of the services running on it.

title: Only Two Countries Can Still Claim Antarctica
summary: CGP Grey explains the history and legal status of territorial claims on Antarctica. It covers the overlapping national claims and the Antarctic Treaty that freezes them.

title: Winning at programming competitions is a negative factor for being good on the job
summary: A one-minute clip of Peter Norvig saying that Google found programming contest success correlates negatively or poorly with job performance. The description links to a blog post discussing it.

title: Quantum Computing and Bitcoin (Vitalik Buterin, November 2013)
summary: A 2013 lecture in which Vitalik Buterin explains what quantum computers are and what they can and cannot do. He then discusses what they could mean for Bitcoin's cryptography.

title: Q&A: Techniques for dealing with lack of motivation, malaise, depression
summary: The question-and-answer session that followed Jonathan Blow's talk on dealing with lack of motivation, malaise and depression. It is hosted on YouTube as a mirror of a Twitch recording.

title: World's Second Best Speakers!
summary: Tech Ingredients builds a pair of large Voigt speakers and explains ported, transmission line and horn designs. It tests them in an anechoic chamber and uses constrained layer damping for the enclosure.

title: Keynote. Fortress Features and Lessons Learned | Guy Steele | JuliaCon 2016
summary: Guy Steele's JuliaCon 2016 keynote on the Fortress language, its features and the lessons learned from the project.

title: 34C3 -  Console Security - Switch
summary: A 34C3 talk on the security architecture of the Nintendo Switch and the early progress breaking it. It introduces the Switch's custom OS and software stack, with the hackers' reverse-engineering and glitching work.

title: Human brain mapping and brain decoding. | Jack Gallant | TEDxSanFrancisco
summary: Berkeley neuroscientist Jack Gallant shows how fMRI brain mapping can be used to decode what a person sees, with visualizations of brain activity and its implications.

title: Optional - The Mother of All Bikesheds by Stuart Marks
summary: Stuart Marks explains the intended purpose and proper use of Java 8's Optional class and why it caused so much controversy. He gives guidelines for using its small API correctly.

title: IPv6 Summit 2014: Wells Fargo adopting IPv6
summary: Wells Fargo engineers walk through the bank's four-year IPv6 journey at the North American IPv6 Summit 2014. They cover motivation, approach, achievements and observations.

title: 5 REAL Possibilities for Interstellar Travel
summary: PBS Space Time surveys five realistic options for interstellar travel, from conventional rocket fuel to antimatter and nuclear pulse propulsion. The options rely only on known physics.

title: Keynote: The Road To LiveView 1.0 by Chris McCord | ElixirConf EU 2023
summary: Chris McCord's ElixirConf EU 2023 keynote tracing LiveView's evolution from simple form validation to full apps, with code examples and live demos of what 1.0 will offer.

title: NYCBSDCon 2014: Serving one-third of the Internet via FreeBSD
summary: Scott Long of Netflix presents the architecture of the OpenConnect content delivery network at NYCBSDCon 2014. He explains why Netflix runs FreeBSD 10 on its appliances and what the future holds.

title: iPhone 12 Anti Repair Design - Teardown and Repair Assessment
summary: Hugh Jeffreys tears down the iPhone 12 and assesses its repairability, focusing on how parts are serialized and tied to the device so swapping components between phones does not work.

title: The Computer Designed To Die In Microseconds
summary: Scott Manley tells the story of a computerized telemetry system built to sit at the heart of a nuclear test device in place of the plutonium pit, designed to transmit data in the microseconds before it was destroyed.

title: DConf 2019: All Spreadsheets Must Die -- Robert Schadek
summary: A DConf 2019 talk by Robert Schadek arguing that spreadsheets are the world's dominant programming language and that D can be used to replace them. It looks at spreadsheet quirks and then at techniques for moving away from them.

title: John Backus: Function Level Programming and the FL Language 1987
summary: A 1987 talk in which John Backus, creator of Fortran, presents function-level programming and the FL language, a successor to his FP work. It is an archival recording with links to the related paper.

title: The TRUTH About How LTT Makes Money
summary: Linus Tech Tips breaks down the company's income streams, including sponsors, YouTube Premium, merch and other products. It gives percentages for each revenue source.

title: Making Humans a Multiplanetary Species
summary: Elon Musk's 2016 IAC presentation on the technical challenges and architectures for building a self-sustaining human presence on Mars.

title: "Focusing is about saying no" - Steve Jobs (WWDC'97)
summary: A three-minute clip of Steve Jobs at WWDC 1997 explaining that focus means saying no to many good ideas. It is a short answer about product strategy and its effect on people.

title: Guy Kawasaki: The Top 10 Mistakes of Entrepreneurs
summary: Guy Kawasaki's UC Berkeley Haas talk on the top ten mistakes entrepreneurs make, covering a startup from inception to exit.

title: Dr. Chris Mack Toasts the End of Moore's Law at SPIE Advanced Lithography 2014
summary: A brief toast by lithography expert Chris Mack at SPIE Advanced Lithography 2014, humorously declaring the end of Moore's Law. His argument centers on the cost per transistor no longer falling.

title: R. P. Feynman on social sciences
summary: A two-minute clip of Richard Feynman on the social sciences, discussing what counts as real science versus pseudo science.

title: Interfacing D To Legacy C++ Code
summary: Walter Bright explains to the Northwest C++ Users Group how the D programming language can interface directly with legacy C++ code. He covers why C++ is hard to interface with and how D approaches the problem.

title: Breaking the 1000ms Time to Glass Mobile Barrier
summary: Ilya Grigorik of Google's Make the Web Fast team explains how to build a mobile site that appears on screen within one second. He covers the network and rendering constraints on mobile.

title: Lies on the London Underground
summary: Tom Scott and Matt Parker investigate some of the small deceptions and oddities of the London Underground, such as misleading signage and map distortions.

title: The Big Lie About Nuclear Waste
summary: Cleo Abram's explainer on whether nuclear waste is really the intractable problem it is portrayed as, looking at how spent fuel can be recycled and used. It features a collaboration with Johnny Harris.

title: How Steve Jobs got the ideas of GUI from XEROX
summary: A short video telling how Xerox PARC invented the graphical user interface and how Steve Jobs's 1979 visit influenced Apple's Lisa.

title: How to Heat a Swimming Pool with an Air Conditioner | Ask This Old House
summary: A This Old House segment where Richard Trethewey installs a heat exchanger that uses waste heat from a central air conditioner to heat a swimming pool.

title: Resveratrol – The Unfortunate (& Scandalous) Story
summary: Dr Brad Stanfield recounts the research history and scandal around resveratrol, the supposed anti-aging supplement, including problems with the original studies.

title: Inspiring a future Clojure editor with forgotten Lisp UX - Shaun Lebron
summary: Shaun Lebron surveys 50 years of Lisp editing history and forgotten innovations in structural editing. He argues future Clojure editors could learn from them, and covers ideas like Parinfer.

title: Building AI Silicon
summary: Jim Keller, CTO of Tenstorrent, talks at Samsung Foundry's SAFE 2021 about building AI silicon through modular, provable design. The talk also touches on Tenstorrent's RISC-V Ascalon core.

title: Why did Netflix use NGINX and FreeBSD to build their own CDN? by Gleb Smirnoff
summary: Gleb Smirnoff explains why Netflix built its own CDN on FreeBSD and NGINX, and how Netflix and NGINX Inc. collaborate on the software. It is a conference talk about open-source choices for video delivery.

title: Steve Jobs - NeXT marketing strategy video 1991
summary: An internal 1991 NeXT video in which Steve Jobs explains the company's product and marketing strategy. It shows NeXT aiming at the Unix workstation market.

title: Containers and Steam: Putting games under pressure | FOSDEM 2020
summary: FOSDEM 2020 talk from Collabora on pressure-vessel, an experimental mechanism that puts Steam games in containers on Linux. It covers using namespaces to give games their own runtime library stack independent of the host.

title: Noam Chomsky  Thought Control In Democratic Societies  NEW!
summary: A lecture by Noam Chomsky on thought control in democratic societies, covering propaganda and manufacturing consent. The upload has no description.

title: Juvenoia
summary: Vsauce looks at 'juvenoia', the exaggerated fear that new media and youth culture are corrupting the young. It gives historical examples of older generations complaining about the next one.

title: How to stop screwing yourself over | Mel Robbins | TEDxSF
summary: Mel Robbins gives a TEDxSF talk on why people sabotage themselves and how to push past hesitation. It is the source of her 'count backward from five' technique.

title: WWDC24: Go small with Embedded Swift | Apple
summary: An Apple WWDC24 session introducing Embedded Swift, a subset of Swift with no runtime that targets tiny microcontrollers. It demonstrates the idea on an off-the-shelf Matter smart home device.

title: Why Photos of the Eiffel Tower at Night are Illegal
summary: Half as Interesting explains why the Eiffel Tower's night-time lighting is under copyright, which makes publishing photos of it at night legally problematic.

title: Abusing YouTube Copyright Claims (Tutorial)
summary: The Original Ace shows how creators can use a third-party music distributor to file Content ID claims on their own videos, turning false-claim abuse into a share of ad revenue. It also names distribution companies and their revenue splits.

title: Trace Driven Development: Unifying Testing and Observability - Ted Young, LightStep
summary: Ted Young of LightStep proposes trace testing, using distributed tracing data to unify testing and observability. The KubeCon-era talk argues for testing against trace data rather than treating tests and monitoring separately.

title: AI Succession
summary: A short pre-recorded talk by Rich Sutton for the World AI Conference in Shanghai arguing that succession from humanity to AI is inevitable. He lays out his view of that transition.

title: Brother Printer Genuine Toner Fix - Use Any Toner
summary: A short walkthrough of a hack that tricks a Brother laser printer into accepting third-party toner by working around its genuine-toner check. It notes this may void the warranty.

title: Europe Is Actually Five Different Groups of Countries
summary: A short CGP Grey explainer on the overlapping and inconsistent membership arrangements of European countries across the EU, Schengen, the euro and the EEA. It shows why "the EU" is full of exceptions.

title: Origins of the Apple Human Interface
summary: A 1997 Computer History Museum lecture in which Larry Tesler and Chris Espinosa recount how the Apple human interface was born, from the Lisa through the Macintosh. It covers design decisions such as discoverability and the standard editing keys.

title: DEF CON 23 - Charlie Miller & Chris Valasek - Remote Exploitation of an Unaltered Passenger Vehicle
summary: Charlie Miller and Chris Valasek present their DEF CON 23 talk on remotely compromising an unmodified Jeep, pivoting from the entertainment system to the vehicle's internal networks to send control messages. They aim to show the reality of car hacking.

title: Making Microchips at Home - Cooking with Jeri Part1
summary: Jeri Ellsworth shows early steps of making microchips at home: cleaving wafers, removing native oxide, testing dopant type with a hot probe, and loading the furnace.

title: Why Does Portuguese Sound Like Russian?! (or Polish)
summary: A Langfocus video examining why Portuguese, especially European Portuguese, sounds like Russian or Polish. It compares shared sounds such as vowel reduction and palatalization.

title: Sky: An Experiment Writing Dart for Mobile (Dart Developer Summit 2015)
summary: Eric Seidel presents Sky, an experimental open-source framework for writing mobile apps in Dart with fast development cycles and 60Hz UI. Sky later became Flutter.

title: Twitter’s Quest for a Wholly Graal Runtime by Chris Thalinger
summary: Chris Thalinger of Twitter describes the company's effort to run its Scala services on the Graal JIT compiler at Scala Days NYC 2018. It covers the performance gains Twitter saw and the work of running Graal in production.

title: DR. QUANTUM - DOUBLE SLIT EXPERIMENT
summary: A short animated lesson, featuring Dr. Quantum, on the double slit experiment and how observing electrons seems to change their behavior.

title: Kraut Space Magic: the H&K G11
summary: Forgotten Weapons examines the Heckler & Koch G11, a West German experimental rifle built around a caseless cartridge. The video covers the G11K2 and its unusual technology before its cancellation for political and economic reasons.

title: Cloaking
summary: Matt Cutts of Google explains what cloaking is: serving different content to search engine crawlers than to users. He covers why it violates Google's webmaster guidelines.

title: How to Slow Aging (and even reverse it)
summary: Veritasium presents David Sinclair's information theory of aging, which says aging is a loss of epigenetic information, and the evidence that aging can be slowed or reversed. It touches on stressors like fasting, exercise and cold exposure.

title: Lars Bergstrom - Beyond Safety and Speed: How Rust Fuels Team Productivity
summary: Lars Bergstrom of Google presents how Rust improves team productivity beyond safety and speed, with data on rewrites, defects and review. It compares Rust teams to those on legacy native languages and Go.

title: Breaking Conventions with The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
summary: A 2017 GDC session in which Nintendo's Breath of the Wild team walks through how the game's convention-breaking systems were built. It covers the 'chemistry engine' of material interactions and shows the early 2D prototype footage.

title: The Next Programming Language - Douglas Crockford - code::dive 2022
summary: Douglas Crockford's code::dive 2022 talk on what the next programming language should look like. He presents ideas behind his Misty language, including message-passing actors.

title: The Contradictions of Battery Operated Vehicles  | Graham Conway | TEDxSanAntonio
summary: A TEDx talk arguing that battery electric vehicles are not as environmentally friendly as commonly believed and that the rush to adopt them is misguided. TED flagged it as containing claims that lack scientific support.

title: Civilization starter kit | Marcin Jakubowski | TEDxKC
summary: Marcin Jakubowski of Open Source Ecology presents his plan to open-source blueprints for 50 cheap, buildable farming tools, a "civilization starter kit". He argues that opening the means of production can enable self-sustaining lives.

title: Hazard perception test 2026: official DVSA guide
summary: The UK DVSA's one-minute guide to the hazard perception part of the driving theory test, covering when to click and how to score well.

title: Does Hot Water Freeze Faster Than Cold Water?
summary: Sciencium examines the Mpemba effect, the claim that hot water freezes faster than cold water. It walks through experiments and a published paper questioning the effect.

title: Is America Actually Metric?
summary: Veritasium explains that the US signed the Metre Convention in 1875 and that all US customary units are officially defined in terms of metric standards. It also touches on the standard kilogram.

title: Harry Potter By Balenciaga | Step by Step Tutorial
summary: A step-by-step tutorial on making a Harry Potter by Balenciaga style AI video, using tools such as ChatGPT, Midjourney and Eleven Labs for script, images and voices.

title: Bob Martin   SOLID Principles of Object Oriented and Agile Design
summary: Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob) gives a talk on the SOLID principles of object-oriented and agile design, in the context of encapsulation and clean code.

title: The touch lamp; a neat idea, and older than you'd think!
summary: Technology Connections explains how touch lamps work and traces them back through patents to the 1950s, far earlier than most people assume.

title: Massscanning the Internet - Defcon 22 (2014)
summary: A DEF CON 22 panel with Rob Graham, Paul McMillan and Dan Tentler on the quirks of scanning the entire internet with masscan. They discuss how fast IPv4 can be scanned and what the results reveal.

title: The History of Europe: Every Year
summary: An animated map showing the borders and populations of European countries for every year since 400 BC. Vassal states and colonies are excluded from population counts.

title: Preparing for scoped storage (Android Dev Summit '19)
summary: A 2019 Android Dev Summit session on the scoped storage model in Android 10. It gives a plan overview and best practices for apps adapting to the new restrictions.

title: Cynthia Kenyon: Experiments that hint of longer lives
summary: TED talk by biochemist Cynthia Kenyon on how a simple genetic mutation can double the lifespan of the worm C. elegans, and what that suggests about extending healthy human life.

title: The Editor of a Lifetime
summary: Perry Metzger, an Emacs user since 1983, gives a talk on why he has used one editor for decades. It mixes history, philosophy and speculation about Emacs's future, and teaches some Emacs fundamentals.

title: The Only* Car-Free Neighbourhood in Canada (and why you can't live there)
