summary: Not Just Bikes visits the Toronto Islands, home to Canada's only car-free neighbourhood. He explains the waiting list and strict ownership rules and asks why more such places aren't built.

title: The NEW Warp Drive Possibilities
summary: PBS Space Time explains how general relativity permits warp drive in principle and covers recent theoretical advances toward solving the negative energy problem.

title: The One-Decade Task: Putting std::atomic in CUDA. - Olivier Giroux - CppCon 2019
summary: Olivier Giroux's CppCon 2019 talk recounts the roughly ten-year effort to bring std::atomic and the C++ memory model to CUDA GPUs, through ten stories from that work.

title: Exploring Sid Meier's Pirates! - BASIC Code, Quirks, Bugs on Commodore 64
summary: 8-Bit Show And Tell walks through the BASIC source code of the original Commodore 64 Sid Meier's Pirates!. It covers bugs, quirks and traces of abandoned features and scenarios left in the code.

title: AppSec EU15 - Rory Mccune - Security And Modern Software Deployment
summary: Rory McCune's AppSec EU 2015 talk on security risks in modern software deployment. It covers weaknesses in package ecosystems like npm, RubyGems and PyPI, and repository compromise.

title: JVMLS 2015 - Compilers are Databases
summary: Martin Odersky's JVM Language Summit 2015 talk argues that compilers can be thought of as databases. It describes design ideas for the Scala compiler and for developer tools.

title: Why Heathrow Airport Had Empty Flights to Nowhere
summary: Half as Interesting explains why airlines flew empty 'ghost flights' out of Heathrow to keep their landing slots under use-it-or-lose-it rules.

title: Steve Jobs Quoting Alan Kay
summary: A short excerpt from the 2007 iPhone launch where Steve Jobs quotes Alan Kay: people serious about software should make their own hardware. It explains part of why Apple built the phone itself.

title: Michael Jordan's Basketball Hall of Fame Enshrinement Speech
summary: Michael Jordan's 2009 Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame enshrinement speech, in which he thanks and also airs grievances about people who doubted him. It is known for his stories of using slights as motivation.

title: How we're building the Arc Browser Windows app with *Swift*
summary: The Browser Company's CTO explains how the team is building the Arc browser for Windows using Swift. It covers the de-risking work and why they believe it is feasible.

title: Clay Shirky on Love, Internet Style
summary: A short Supernova 2007 provocation in which Clay Shirky uses a 1300-year-old Japanese shrine, rebuilt periodically, as a metaphor for how networks change business and collective creativity.

title: This Town Did The Impossible
summary: A look at Le Plessis-Robinson, a French suburb transformed from modernist urbanism into traditional mixed-use fabric with local-style architecture, green space and a more balanced housing supply.

title: How Netflix Uses Java - 2025 Edition
summary: A Netflix engineer describes how Netflix uses Java in 2025, including Spring Boot, DGS/GraphQL, gRPC and keeping over 3000 services on the latest JDK. It covers generational ZGC upgrade experiences.

title: 37C3 -  Breaking "DRM" in Polish trains
summary: A 37C3 talk on how a series of Polish electric trains stopped working after servicing by an independent company. The speakers explain how train control systems work and how they reverse-engineered the software lockouts.

title: JVMLS 2015 - Java Goes AOT
summary: Christian Thalinger presents at the 2015 JVM Language Summit on adding ahead-of-time compilation to the JVM, covering the HotSpot team's AOT work and its relation to warmup and deoptimization.

title: The Eleventh HOPE (2016): Coding by Voice with Open Source Speech Recognition
summary: A HOPE XI talk on programming by voice with open source speech recognition. The speaker writes Linux systems code by voice and describes building custom voice grammars as an alternative to the keyboard for programmers with repetitive strain injuries.

title: The Algebra of Algebraic Data Types
summary: A London Haskell talk on the algebra of algebraic data types, showing how sum and product types behave like arithmetic. It frames types as numbers obeying algebraic laws.

title: The 'duck curve' is solar energy's greatest challenge
summary: A short Vox explainer on the duck curve, the shape electricity demand takes in California as solar output grows. It explains why grid operators struggle to balance supply and demand with lots of solar.

title: Decentralized Web Summit - Live From The Internet Archive
summary: Full-day livestream of the 2016 Decentralized Web Summit at the Internet Archive, with speakers including Vint Cerf, Tim Berners-Lee, Brewster Kahle, Cory Doctorow and Mitchell Baker. It explores the technology and impact of a decentralized web.

title: This library has every book ever published.
summary: Tom Scott visits the British Library, a UK legal deposit library that receives a copy of everything published, and discusses storing so much material, including the web archive.

title: Superblocks: How Barcelona is taking city streets back from cars
summary: A short Vox video on Barcelona's superblocks, an urban design approach that closes interior streets to through traffic to return space to pedestrians.

title: Lang NEXT 2014 Panel  Systems Programming in 2014 and Beyond
summary: A panel from the Lang NEXT 2014 conference on systems programming in 2014 and beyond. Language designers including Bjarne Stroustrup and Rob Pike discuss the topic, including C++ header compile times.

title: The Most COMPLEX Pop Song of All Time
summary: Rick Beato analyzes a pop song he argues is among the most harmonically complex ever, breaking down its chords and key changes. It is a music theory deep dive aimed at general music fans.

title: Inequality: Why are the rich getting richer?
summary: A three-minute Positive Money UK explainer arguing that the commercial banking system, where banks create most money as debt, redistributes income from the bottom 90 percent to the top 10 percent through interest.

title: The highway where trucks work like electric trains
summary: Tom Scott visits an eHighway test in Lubeck, Germany, where electric trucks with pantographs draw power from overhead wires. He explains how this could electrify road freight.

title: GPT3: An Even Bigger Language Model - Computerphile
summary: Rob Miles discusses GPT-3 on Computerphile, covering how scaling parameters kept improving results over GPT-2 and how the model nearly learned arithmetic without anyone knowing exactly how.

title: I can't show you how pink this pink is.
summary: Tom Scott explains why a vivid pink pigment by artist Stuart Semple cannot be fully shown on a screen, and touches on the dispute over exclusive rights to the blackest black pigment. It is a short explainer on color gamuts and pigment politics.

title: Polyworld: Using Evolution to Design Artificial Intelligence
summary: A 2007 Google Tech Talk introducing Polyworld, an artificial life simulator used to evolve artificial intelligence by designing worlds rather than minds. It presents results from ongoing attempts to evolve intelligent behavior.

title: Serving Netflix Video at 400Gbps on FreeBSD by Drew Gallatin
summary: Netflix engineer Drew Gallatin explains how Netflix serves TLS-encrypted video at 400Gb/s from a single FreeBSD server. He covers NUMA, kernel TLS, hardware TLS offload and the memory bandwidth and PCIe bottlenecks they hit.

title: Comparing Beta & VHS on Quality: Was Beta Really Better?
summary: Technology Connections compares Betamax and VHS picture quality using footage from a 1979 RCA VCR and argues the Beta quality advantage was largely marketing.

title: Mark Fisher : The Slow Cancellation Of The Future
summary: Mark Fisher's 2014 talk in Zagreb on the slow cancellation of the future, about cultural stagnation and the sense that popular culture has stopped producing the new.

title: Sound of the dialup modem explained
summary: A short animation that pairs the sound of a dialup modem handshake with a graphic explaining what each phase of the sound means.

title: Gerald Jay Sussman: The Role of Programming   (Dan Friedman's 60th Birthday)
summary: Gerald Jay Sussman speaks at Dan Friedman's 60th birthday celebration about how programming helps formulate and clarify ideas. He argues that ambiguous mathematical notation hinders understanding.

title: Anthony Marcar - Clojure At Scale @WalmartLabs
summary: Anthony Marcar describes lessons from three years of using Clojure at WalmartLabs, including scaling a team and a large multi-project codebase in an enterprise setting.

title: Why You Can't Name A File CON In Windows
summary: Tom Scott explains why Windows does not let you name a file CON, tracing the reserved device names back to backwards compatibility with DOS.

title: The Best Kind of Dutch Cycling Infrastructure
summary: Not Just Bikes explains Dutch bicycle-only roads, which let people travel long distances in and out of cities with almost no car interaction. It shows how this changes cycling from a chore into something enjoyable.

title: The single biggest reason why start-ups succeed | Bill Gross | TED
summary: Bill Gross, who has founded and incubated many start-ups, ranked hundreds of companies on five factors. He presents the one factor that stood out as the biggest predictor of success.

title: The Shotgun Booby Trap (The Case Of)
summary: LegalEagle analyzes Katko v. Briney, the Iowa case about a homeowner whose shotgun booby trap injured a burglar, and the limits on deadly force in defending property.

title: Surge 2015 - Lightning Talks
summary: A collection of lightning talks from the Surge 2015 conference on scalable systems, hosted by Geir Magnusson. HN mostly points to one segment, a Bryan Cantrill talk touching on madvise semantics.

title: Jujutsu: A Git-Compatible VCS - Git Merge 2022
summary: Martin von Zweigbergk presents Jujutsu (jj), a Git-compatible VCS with undo, anonymous branches, first-class conflicts, automatic rebasing, and the working copy as a commit. He also covers plans at Google.

title: Why Traffic Congestion Grows Exponentially, Why It Matters, and What To Do About It // An Explainer
summary: CityNerd explains why traffic congestion grows nonlinearly as more cars use a road network, and why adding road capacity tends not to fix it. It covers the consequences for drivers, bus riders, cyclists and pedestrians, and discusses alternatives such as true bus rapid transit.

title: How a Diesel-Electric Locomotive Works
summary: A 3D-animated walkthrough of a heavy-haul diesel-electric freight locomotive, covering the frame, coupling, draft gear, engine and drive systems. Made in Blender by Animagraffs.

title: The Tube Map nearly looked very different
summary: Map Men's Jay Foreman tells the story of how the London Tube map nearly looked very different, including Harry Beck's design and TfL's initial rejection of it. A short, witty history of a design icon.

title: Porting KVM to SmartOS - Brian Cantrill, Joyent, KVM Forum 2011
summary: Bryan Cantrill of Joyent describes the experience of porting KVM to SmartOS, an Illumos-based OS, at KVM Forum 2011. He covers the process, the pain points and how DTrace helped.

title: The food we were born to eat: John McDougall at TEDxFremont
summary: Dr. John McDougall argues at TEDxFremont that starch-based diets are what humans were born to eat, drawing on 40 years of nutrition and disease work.

title: T-Mobile's journey to IPv6
summary: Stephan Lagerholm of T-Mobile explains at NANOG how T-Mobile turned off IPv4 for over 10 million handsets using DNS64 and related technologies. He shares advice on finding and handling broken applications.

title: Hydrogen vs. Battery Electric Cars
summary: Physics Girl compares hydrogen fuel cell cars and battery electric cars after driving 1800 miles in a Toyota Mirai. The video was part of a series sponsored by Toyota.

title: Double Pendulums are Chaoticn't
summary: A short explainer from 2swap on the chaotic behavior of double pendulums. It examines how predictable the system is for some starting conditions and whether closed-form solutions exist.

title: The Netherlands Is Not 'Holland.' It Never Was.
summary: A short CGP Grey explainer on why 'Holland' is wrong as a name for the whole country of the Netherlands. It covers the country's provinces and its constituent territories.

title: An Earthshaking Announcement
summary: Donald Knuth gives a talk at Stanford, recorded by Zeeba TV for the TeX Users Group, titled An Earthshaking Announcement.

title: Gas stoves aren't really that fast - even standard electric is faster!
summary: Technology Connections tests how quickly gas, induction and standard electric stoves boil water, with CO2 measurements and a discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of each.

title: Ben Kreuter   RWC 2017
summary: A Real World Crypto 2017 talk by a Google engineer on using private set intersection to match ad views with in-store purchases. It describes privacy-preserving matching that avoids exposing personal transactions.

title: Richard Stallman: Copyright vs. Community
summary: A 2012 lecture by Richard Stallman at Reykjavik University arguing that copyright, built for the printing press, fits poorly with computer networks. He criticizes draconian enforcement and corporate lobbying.

title: Keynote: Greg Kroah-Hartman (Linux Foundation) - "I Don't Want Your Code"
summary: Greg Kroah-Hartman's Linaro keynote on contributing to the Linux kernel, explaining why maintainers prefer upstreamed code and how they view contributions.

title: World's Strongest Magnet!
summary: Veritasium visits the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory to see the world's strongest magnets and demonstrate effects like eddy currents. It covers what intense magnetic fields do to materials and objects.

title: Bringing Types to Elixir by Giuseppe Castagna and Guillaume Duboc | ElixirConf EU 2023
summary: ElixirConf EU 2023 talk by Giuseppe Castagna and Guillaume Duboc on bringing set-theoretic types to Elixir, and the benefits such a type system could offer such as catching bugs.

title: Why is Life the Way it Is? with Nick Lane
summary: Nick Lane's Royal Institution lecture on the origin of life and why it is the way it is. It draws on his book The Vital Question and the alkaline hydrothermal vent theory of abiogenesis.

title: David Deutsch: Chemical scum that dream of distant quasars
summary: David Deutsch's TED talk arguing that humanity's survival depends on solving problems through knowledge growth. He frames people as improbable "chemical scum" capable of understanding distant quasars.

title: Steve Jobs Presents to the Cupertino City Council  (6/7/11)
summary: Steve Jobs presents Apple's proposal for a new campus to the Cupertino City Council in June 2011, answering council members' questions about the plan.

title: Superintelligence: Science or Fiction? | Elon Musk & Other Great Minds
summary: A panel from the Beneficial AI 2017 conference moderated by Max Tegmark, with Elon Musk, Stuart Russell, Kurzweil, Hassabis, Harris, Bostrom, Chalmers and others. They discuss likely outcomes of human-level AGI and what outcomes are desirable.

title: Gauge Theory and Inflation: Enlarging the Wu-Yang Dictionary
summary: A talk by Eric Weinstein on gauge theory and its possible application to economics and inflation. It proposes extending the Wu-Yang dictionary into a geometric tool beyond physics.

title: CUFP 2011 Keynote: Pragmatic Haskell (Lennart Augustsson Standard Chartered Bank)
summary: Lennart Augustsson's CUFP 2011 keynote covers using Haskell commercially at Standard Chartered Bank. He discusses non-standard Haskell implementations, including a strict dialect, and weighs strict against lazy evaluation.

title: Rasmus Lerdorf - 25 Years of PHP - phpday 2019
summary: Rasmus Lerdorf marks 25 years of PHP at phpday 2019 with a look at the highlights and lowlights of the language. He argues for upgrading PHP versions, covering performance, static analysis, zero-cost profiling and dead code elimination.

title: Choice, happiness and spaghetti sauce | Malcolm Gladwell
summary: Malcolm Gladwell's TED talk on how Howard Moskowitz found that there is no single perfect spaghetti sauce. He draws a larger point about choice, preference and happiness.

title: How to Break YouTube (Copyright Claim your own video)
summary: A guide to using YouTube's Content ID by claiming your own videos through a distributor, so the claims share revenue with the creator and monetize re-uploads. It credits another creator who pioneered the method.

title: Tesla AI Day 2021
summary: Tesla's 2021 AI Day presentation covering vision, planning and control, auto-labeling, simulation, the Dojo training hardware and the Tesla Bot announcement, followed by a Q&A.

title: CppCon 2018: G. Nishanov “Nano-coroutines to the Rescue! (Using Coroutines TS, of Course)”
summary: Gor Nishanov's CppCon 2018 talk on using tiny C++ coroutines to hide memory latency, interleaving useful work while prefetches bring cache lines in from main memory.

title: Chiara Mooney & Shiven Mian – Building for Microsoft (Chain React 2023)
summary: Microsoft engineers Chiara Mooney and Shiven Mian describe the journey and challenges of building and consuming React Native for Windows inside Microsoft. It was given at Chain React 2023.

title: The Shortest-Splitline Algorithm: a Gerrymandering Solution [Bonus Video]
summary: A short CGP Grey bonus video explaining the shortest-splitline algorithm, which draws electoral districts by repeatedly splitting a state along its shortest dividing line while balancing population. It is offered as a neutral, algorithmic fix for gerrymandering.

title: The Johns Hopkins Foreign Affairs Symposium Presents: The Price of Privacy: Re-Evaluating the NSA
summary: A Johns Hopkins Foreign Affairs Symposium debate between former NSA and CIA director Michael Hayden and constitutional law professor David Cole, moderated by Major Garrett. They argue over NSA surveillance, its constitutionality and the balance between privacy and security.

title: An elevator that actually goes sideways
summary: Tom Scott visits ThyssenKrupp's test tower in Rottweil to see the Multi, a rope-free elevator that uses linear motors to move cabins sideways as well as vertically.

title: On Bullsh*t Jobs | David Graeber | Meaningless Jobs | Royal Society of Arts | Lecture
summary: David Graeber's RSA lecture on bullshit jobs, expanding on his essay about why so many people do work they believe is pointless. He discusses what this says about the modern economy and the way society values work.

title: The Counterintuitive Physics of Turning a Bike
summary: A two-minute minutephysics video explaining why turning a bicycle requires first steering briefly the other way. It covers counter-steering and balance with slow-motion footage and 3D animation.

title: Innovation Agenda | Barack Obama | Talks at Google
summary: Barack Obama, then a presidential candidate, presents his innovation agenda at Google and takes questions from Eric Schmidt and employees in November 2007.

title: I visited the US National Helium Reserve
summary: Tom Scott visits the US National Helium Reserve in Amarillo, Texas, and explains why headlines that the world is running out of helium are misleading. He covers the Federal Helium Program and its planned privatization.

title: Lars Bak - The Making of a Secure and Robust IoT Development Platform
summary: A Curry On talk by Lars Bak, known for V8 and Dart, on building a secure and robust IoT development platform. It discusses language and VM design choices for small devices.

title: Thomas Sowell on the Myths of Economic Inequality
summary: Thomas Sowell speaks at the Hoover Institution about economic and racial inequality and what he considers myths about poverty. He also recounts his early life and brief flirtation with Marxism.

title: The '5kg in 50 days' Diet!
summary: Thunderf00t applies a simple energy mass balance to weight loss, showing how much exercise is needed to burn off extra calories compared with eating less. He concludes that cutting intake is the easier route and that hunger fades after the first week.

title: The Next Five Years of ClojureScript - David Nolen
summary: David Nolen reviews the first five years of ClojureScript, documenting its landmarks and looking ahead to the next five. It is a history-and-roadmap talk from the Clojure community.

title: Why Swiss Trains are the Best in Europe
summary: Not Just Bikes explains why Swiss trains are considered among the best in Europe and the world, covering frequency, connections and what riding them is like.

title: OSCON 2011:  Karen Sandler
summary: Karen Sandler, then Executive Director of the GNOME Foundation, talks at OSCON 2011 about the risks of proprietary, closed-source software in implanted medical devices like her own pacemaker-defibrillator.

title: Why don't subtitles match dubbing?
summary: Tom Scott explains why subtitles often differ from dubbed dialogue, covering how translation, timing and reading speed shape each. It features translators and voice talent working in several languages.

title: Tea and Consent
summary: A short animation from Thames Valley Police that explains sexual consent by comparing it to offering someone a cup of tea.

title: The Most Extreme Explosion in the Universe
summary: A Kurzgesagt animation on supernovae, the most powerful explosions in the universe. It explains their role in creating elements and what would happen to Earth if one occurred nearby.

title: Why Democracy Is Mathematically Impossible
summary: Veritasium explains why no voting system can be perfectly fair, drawing on Arrow's theorem and the work of Eric Maskin. It looks at problems with systems like first-past-the-post and ranked-choice voting.

title: Cars Are A Disaster For Society -- Here Are the Numbers
summary: CityNerd's Ray Delahanty tallies the personal costs of driving and then the externalities that car dependency imposes on everyone else, with numbers for each. It is an urbanist case that driving is heavily subsidized and costs society far more than drivers pay.

title: Rhonda Patrick:  Nutrigenomics, Epigenetics, and Stress Tolerance
summary: Rhonda Patrick gives an IHMC talk on how genetic variation affects micronutrient absorption and metabolism, and how diet changes gene expression. It also covers epigenetics, including heritable changes, and stress tolerance.

title: What If Dark Matter Is Just Black Holes?
summary: PBS Space Time asks whether dark matter could be made of primordial black holes. It walks through the observational constraints that limit this idea.
primary_topic: dark matter and primordial black holes

title: Capsicum: Practical Capabilities for UNIX
summary: Robert Watson presents the Capsicum paper at USENIX Security 2010, describing practical capability-based sandboxing for UNIX. The paper won Best Student Paper.

title: The surprising decline in violence | Steven Pinker
summary: Steven Pinker's TED talk charts the long decline of violence from biblical times to today, arguing that despite Iraq and Darfur we may be living in the most peaceful era of our species.

title: Clayton Christensen: Disruptive innovation
channel: Saïd Business School, University of Oxford
summary: Clayton Christensen explains his theory of disruptive innovation at Oxford's Said Business School, using examples from steel, Toyota, Sony, Walmart and Godrej. He applies the theory to why some economies stagnate and others grow.

title: Can Japanese Actually Write Japanese Kanji?
summary: Yuta asks whether native Japanese speakers can actually write kanji by hand, showing that many struggle to recall characters from memory.

title: The tech which can charge an electric car in 10 minutes
summary: Technology Connections explains how modern EV fast charging can fill a battery in about 10 to 20 minutes, covering charging standards and EV road trips.

title: "Clojure in Unity 3D: Functional Video Game Development" by Ramsey Nasser and Tims Gardner
summary: A Strange Loop talk presenting an open-source library that integrates Clojure into the Unity 3D game engine. It covers REPL-based live coding, macros, DSLs and persistent data structures for game development.

title: Does AI Actually Boost Developer Productivity? (100k Devs Study) - Yegor Denisov-Blanch, Stanford
summary: Yegor Denisov-Blanch of Stanford presents a study of nearly 100,000 developers at hundreds of companies, measuring how AI affects productivity from commit data. It finds an average boost of about 20% with wide variance by codebase, task complexity and stack.

title: Milton Friedman - Monopoly
summary: A short clip of Milton Friedman explaining his free-market view of monopoly, namely that monopolies persist mainly through government help. It is excerpted from the Milton Friedman Speaks series.

title: How I Animated This Video
summary: Animator Joel Haver explains how he makes his short films using rotoscoping and the EbSynth tool, along with the software he uses. The method is a labor-intensive, frame-by-frame process.

title: GopherCon 2014 Inside the Gophers Studio with Blake Mizerany
summary: A GopherCon 2014 session where Blake Mizerany replaced his planned talk with a panel discussion with members of the Go team. It covers Go's design choices and community questions.

title: ElixirConf 2019 - Day 1 Morning Keynote - Brian Cardarella, Luke Imhoff, Paul Schoenfelder
summary: The ElixirConf 2019 day 1 morning keynote, including the announcement of Lumen, an alternative BEAM implementation designed for WebAssembly. It features DockYard's team presenting the project and a demo.

title: Scala Collections: Why Not?
summary: Paul Phillips, a Typesafe co-founder and prolific Scala committer, explains why he walked away from Scala. He critiques the Scala collections library and presents his own design focused on immutability, performance and correctness.

title: Rob Pike about the target group of the Go programming language (golang)
summary: A short excerpt of Rob Pike's Lang.NEXT 2014 talk where he describes Go's target audience as young Google programmers who are not researchers. The language has to be easy for them to understand and adopt.

title: Your Home Can Survive a Wildfire
summary: NFPA video in which wildfire researcher Jack Cohen explains that embers (firebrands), not the flame front, are the main cause of homes igniting in wildfires. He shows how landscaping and removing debris around the home reduce risk.

title: LED Christmas lights still annoy me. Let's try some more fixes.
summary: Technology Connections complains about the harsh, overly blue color of modern LED Christmas lights and tries more fixes for them. It follows earlier videos by the same creator on holiday lighting.

title: 'Zombie' Parasite Cordyceps Fungus Takes Over Insects Through Mind Control | National Geographic
summary: National Geographic footage showing the cordyceps fungus infecting ants and other insects and steering their behavior so it can reproduce.

title: Did People Used To Look Older?
summary: Vsauce explores whether people in past decades really looked older than people of the same age today, or whether photographic and cultural factors make them seem so. It draws on old photos, yearbooks and perception research.

title: The astounding athletic power of quadcopters | Raffaello D'Andrea
summary: In a TEDGlobal talk, Raffaello D'Andrea demonstrates quadcopters that play catch, balance, learn and coordinate, using algorithms that treat them like athletes. It includes Kinect-controlled quads.

title: The Longest-Running Evolution Experiment
summary: Veritasium visits Richard Lenski's lab to explain the decades-long E. coli evolution experiment, which asks how repeatable evolution is and shows bacteria evolving to use a new food source.

title: Outside In
summary: A 21-minute animation showing how a sphere can be turned inside out without creases or tears, known as sphere eversion.

title: NIPS 2017 Test of Time Award "Machine learning has become alchemy.” | Ali Rahimi, Google
summary: Ali Rahimi accepts the NIPS 2017 Test of Time Award and argues that machine learning has become alchemy, with practice running ahead of understanding.

title: Why We Should NOT Look For Aliens - The Dark Forest
summary: Kurzgesagt animated explainer on the Dark Forest answer to the Fermi Paradox. It argues that if advanced civilizations exist, staying silent may be the safest strategy because revealing yourself invites a first strike.

title: The Big Short (2015) - Jared Vennett's Pitch to Front Point Partners (Jenga Blocks Scene) [HD 1080p]
summary: A scene from The Big Short in which Jared Vennett pitches credit default swaps on mortgage bonds to a hedge fund team, using a Jenga tower to illustrate collateralized debt obligations.

title: 1 -  L'énergie - Cours des Mines 2019 - Jancovici -  [EN subtitles available]
summary: Part 1 of Jean-Marc Jancovici's 2019 course at Ecole des Mines de Paris, on energy and its central role in the economy and climate. It is in French with English subtitles available and runs about two and a half hours.

title: So you think you can validate email addresses A journey down RFC5321
summary: Stavros Korokithakis gives a FOSDEM 2018 talk on how hard it is to validate email addresses properly, taking a tour through RFC 5321.

title: 35C3 -  How Facebook tracks you on Android
summary: A 35C3 talk by Privacy International researchers who captured and decrypted traffic between Android apps and Facebook servers. They show many apps send Facebook device and usage data immediately on launch, even for users without Facebook accounts.

title: Null References: The Billion Dollar Mistake - Tony Hoare
summary: Tony Hoare's InfoQ talk in which he describes introducing null references in ALGOL W in 1965 and calls it his billion-dollar mistake. He discusses language designer responsibility and run-time checks.

title: Everything About Grain Bins (Farmers are Geniuses) - Smarter Every Day 218
summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day explores how grain bins work and the engineering and know-how involved in farming. His point is that farmers are exceptionally capable.

title: React.js Conf 2015 - Hype!
summary: Ryan Florence's React.js Conf 2015 talk pushes React into unusual use cases, including a demo comparing rendering in React, Ember and Angular.

title: why Japan's internet is weirdly designed
summary: Answer in Progress investigates why Japanese websites look different from those elsewhere, using an AI clustering approach to test the 2013 claim. It then looks at possible explanations.

title: On Mathematical Maturity (1) Thomas Garrity
channel: IAS | PCMI Park City Mathematics Institute
summary: Thomas Garrity discusses mathematical maturity, a concept mathematicians use for professional development, and how it can inform teaching, mentoring and careers. It was given at the IAS/PCMI Park City Mathematics Institute.

title: How to Create a Mind | Ray Kurzweil | Talks at Google
summary: Ray Kurzweil presents his book How to Create a Mind at Google, on reverse engineering the brain and using that understanding to build intelligent machines. He shows his graphs of exponential technological progress.
